pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 15.3.1 AFFIRMATIVE AND NEGATIVE SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.3: Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: When do we use affirmative statements?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. construct affirmative and negative sentences in varied contexts

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences

Teach
• Focus skill: construct affirmative and negative sentences in varied contexts.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. When do we use affirmative statements?
2. When do we use negative statements?
3. Why is it important to use the right sentence when saying something?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
